lead: two finished answers leave your bench for every one that was commissioned. the client asked for a shelf and gets the shelf, and standing beside it the other thing that would also have solved it, built to the same standard.
sun: the fork does not arrive at the drawing stage, where it would be cheap. it arrives at the bench, in timber and hours, because both solutions are real to you at the point where a real object has to be made, and neither has ever been demoted to a sketch. so the workshop runs at half the output of anyone with your hands, and every job in it is late.
moon: and the second one goes out too. it exists, somebody can use it, and The Hand has no price for the half that was not ordered — so it travels in the van beside the invoiced one, unmentioned, and the household receiving two pieces of work for the cost of one has no idea that this is the arrangement.
pull: every job you have ever taken was done twice, properly, and billed once. the second one is usually the better answer, and it left the workshop with nothing on it.
tension: the trade reads your delivery dates the obvious way, and has done for years. a customer waiting eleven weeks does not care that he is waiting for two of something, and the man who quoted six got the work. nobody has ever stood in front of the pair at the end of it and looked at what is there: two finished objects, both correct, made by the person they have all been calling unable to choose.
cost: a problem leaves your hands with two workable ends on it, which nobody else in the trade manages, and the households that got both know what they got. the piece in the exhibition carries another name. it goes to whoever had a single idea in spring and gave the year to it, so they finish six and you finish three, twice.

lead: the thing you are known for was released in two versions in the same year, both finished, both under your name, and the field has spent a decade deciding which one it is going to remember.
sun: picking one at the proof stage was available and would have cost nothing, and it did not happen, because at the proof stage both of them were right and both of them still are. what went out was a pair, offered without a ranking, and a pair cannot be quoted. everybody who has ever wanted to cite you has had to settle it on your behalf, and no two of them have settled it alike.
moon: neither version went out with anything over it. no note naming one authoritative, no line about what either is for, nothing that would tell a reader where to start. covering the work and ranking the work are the same gesture, and this pairing performs neither, so the two of them stand in public bare, and the ranking has been done since by people who had something to sell.
pull: two authorised versions, no ranking on either, and a decade of strangers settling which of them you meant. both were meant. that has never once been sayable in a room that wants one.
tension: an interviewer asks which is the real one, and the answer runs four minutes and loses the room. saying both is available and it sounds like a sales line. a definitive edition would end the business in an afternoon, the publisher has asked twice, and the sentence they need for the front of it is the one thing you have no means of producing. so the readership goes on splitting, and each half believes the other was misled.
cost: anyone who takes the two together gets a range nobody else in the field has put on paper, and three careers have been built on doing exactly that. which version a person knows depends on their teacher. no single object of yours has ever stood in front of the whole audience at once, and nothing is left to make one out of that is not already out there twice.

lead: every faction in a twenty-year argument keeps a list of its own people. you are on neither list, and both sides have been ringing you all week, separately, about the same meeting.
sun: you carry both readings of the dispute at full weight, out loud, in front of whoever is asking. that is not a diplomatic manoeuvre, and nobody hears one. what they hear is membership of the other camp, whichever camp is listening, so each side has you down as a sympathiser of the other, and each file is half right, and nothing you say in a meeting revises either.
moon: nothing in you pushes back on the filing. a person who minded being placed wrongly would go and be seen with the right people for a season, and The Veil issues no such wanting. so the misplacement stands for years, uncontested, and the absence of any protest gets taken by both camps as the last piece of evidence they were waiting for.
pull: both readings of the argument are correct and one person is carrying both. there is no word for that position, so nobody in twenty years has been able to say where you stand.
tension: when the deputy post came up, each side put a name in, and each name had a year of quiet work behind it. that work is what a faction does for its own. nothing was done against you and nobody blocked anything; there was simply no one in the room where names get pushed whose job it was to push yours. you found out about the appointment when the rest of the building did, and were surprised by the surprise.
cost: both rooms tell you things they would not tell each other, and the argument has stayed survivable partly because one person has held an accurate account of both halves of it for two decades. that account has no owner. when the history gets written it will be written by a side, and there is no side whose version you appear in.

lead: there is no second kind of part in here. most people fork somewhere and run straight everywhere else; the branching goes the whole way through this one, so nothing in you has ever run one way.
sun: rooms stop asking you what to do and start asking you to lay it out. the two-sided account is what you are for now, and it is genuinely useful, and it is never the last thing said, because somebody else closes. thirty years of being the most consulted person in the building has produced no decision with your name against it, and nobody reads that as a loss, least of all the people consulting you.
moon: the choosing does happen. it happens twice, and both results get carried out. what other people report afterwards as having gone with their gut comes off an instrument that was never fitted here, so asked what you want, you produce two answers at identical volume and no third thing to rank them with. no moment of being torn ever occurred, which is why you never went looking for the ranking.
pull: two ways at once, and then that again. nothing in you has ever run in a single direction, so you have arrived second at everything you now hold.
tension: the advice has been the same since you were nineteen and it is always pick one. it comes from people who like you, who have watched you take eleven years over something they would have settled in two, and who are treating hesitation. there is none there to treat. the treatment does nothing, its failure gets logged as stubbornness, and by fifty you have stopped explaining, which they take as the confirmation.
cost: you can hold two claims at full weight for a decade without going bitter about either, which almost nobody manages past the first bad year, and it is why the ugly disputes get handed to you. everything you now have was reached late. no sacrifice appears anywhere in your record either, because nothing you have ever done cost you the other option.
